title: Signalised crossroads: circular green with a red right-turn arrow
summary: A north-south road crosses an east-west road under signal control. The ego car approaches northbound behind the RMS2 marking J stop line; the primary head on its approach shows circular green lit with the right-turn arrow red lit (Traffic Police handbook illustration, PDF page 47). One world has the ego intending to turn right, the other going straight. Only the north-south heads exist in the extraction set, so east-west permissions come from the phase plan.

worlds.label: Ego intends to turn right; circular green lit, right arrow red lit
notes: The controller derives permission(ns.with.0.right) = stop from the lit right_arrow_red on ns.nb.head.primary, while circular_green gives ns.with.0.straight and ns.with.0.left proceed_permissive. Nothing is inferred from lens position or artwork.

worlds.label: Ego intends to go straight; circular green lit, right arrow red lit
notes: Same aspect state as the right-turn world; only the ego's declared movement differs, so ev.ego-lane-intent now names ns.with.0.straight, which the circular green permits.

sourceLocator.section: Examples, circular green with red right arrow
sourceLocator.quote: Means “GO” for straight ahead vehicles only. Vehicles turning right must stop behind the stop line.

unknowns: housing dimensions, column spacing and the offset from housing back to any lens centre (raster illustration only)
no official signal support drawing exists in the reviewed collection; the pole is the F0 schematic fallback
horizontal heads have no reviewed artwork and are not modelled
Green 'B' placement conflict between TP page 47 and Rule 11 remains unresolved and is not modelled
stop-line position relative to the signal head is not settled by RMS2 (A1 manifest unresolved note, preserved)

Schematic pole (dimensionsStatus schematic_unsourced). The A2 signal candidate has an empty compatibleSupports list because no official signal support drawing was reviewed; the 2.29 m lens height in the world is the Rule 11 nominal, not a site value.

comparisons.label: Same junction when no right arrow is lit: the circular green then governs the right turn
comparisons.generationNote: Both north-south heads share one controller state, so the delta darkens the arrow on both heads exactly as nsRightArrow=dark does.

comparisons.label: Same junction when the right arrow turns green
comparisons.generationNote: Not regenerated: nsCircular=green with nsRightArrow=green lights a protected right arrow on BOTH heads while the opposing straight movement proceeds, which V1 reports as signal_movements.unsupported_phase_combination (known C2 finding). The declarative delta changes only the northbound head; a comparison applier must give the southbound head a compatible state before this world can pass V1.

comparisons.label: Same junction when the circular light is red

exclusions: Pedestrian crossings and pedestrian signals are not placed: none has been separately sourced.
No east-west signal heads: the extraction set holds one signal head reference, so east-west permissions are asserted by the phase plan with empty governedByAspects (world provenance note, preserved).
No Green 'B', flashing amber, amber-arrow or horizontal-head states are authored; their rules exist in A3 but have no starter fixture or artwork.

sourceRefs.section: Examples, circular green with red right arrow
sourceRefs.quote: Means “GO” for straight ahead vehicles only. Vehicles turning right must stop behind the stop line.
Do not turn right even when there is no traffic from the opposite direction
Look to the right and left to ensure it is safe before you proceed.
the illuminated red arrow light shall be taken as prohibiting vehicles from proceeding beyond the stop line or broken lines on the road in that direction

unresolved: Rule 11 capture ends partway through the green-arrow paragraph; the red-arrow paragraph is complete (A3 rule red-arrow-prohibits-movement unresolved note, preserved).
The handbook illustrates the right arrow only; left and straight-ahead red arrows are not authored.
Signal housing, column spacing, pole height and mount are unknown in the source; poles are schematic and 2.29 m is the Rule 11 nominal lens height, not a site value.
